title: Blackberry and apple cake
subtitle: a soft, moist autumn cake with bramley apple and blackberries folded through a buttermilk sponge
excerpt: Blackberry and apple cake is a traybake-style cake with bramley apple pieces and fresh blackberries folded into a soft buttermilk sponge. The apple softens into the crumb as it bakes and the blackberries burst, leaving deep purple pockets through the cake. It keeps well and the crumb stays moist for three or four days.
sourceNotes: Blackberry and apple as a combination is one of the most traditional British fruit pairings, historically used together in crumbles, pies, and jams from late summer foraging. Incorporating them into a buttermilk cake is a modern home-baking approach that became common in British baking books from the 2000s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cut into portions and wrap individually. Freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 to 4 days. Better the second day.

content.text: Blackberry and apple cake is a soft, deeply fruited traybake with bramley apple and fresh blackberries folded through a simple buttermilk sponge. The apple breaks down into the crumb as it bakes, adding moisture and a slight tartness. The blackberries burst and colour the batter around them. The whole thing is ready in under an hour and needs nothing more than a dusting of icing sugar.

items.prepNote: peeled, cored, cut into 1 cm pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease and line a 20 x 30 cm rectangular baking tin with baking paper.

Beat the softened butter and light brown sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, adding a tablespoon of the flour with each one to prevent curdling. Beat in the vanilla.
Sift in the flour, baking powder, and bicarbonate of soda. Add the buttermilk and fold together until just combined and no dry flour remains. Do not overmix.

Fold in the apple pieces. Spoon the batter into the prepared tin and level the surface. Scatter the blackberries over the top, pressing them lightly into the batter. Scatter the demerara sugar over the surface.

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean and the top is golden. The edges will pull away from the tin slightly. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes before lifting out. Dust with icing sugar if using.

attrs.problem: Cake very wet and sinking in the centre
attrs.avoid: Avoid very ripe or watery blackberries and too much apple; excess moisture prevents the cake from setting.
attrs.fix: Pat the blackberries dry before using. Use a firm, tart cooking apple rather than a soft eating apple. A skewer test is essential as the fruit can make the surface look set while the centre is still wet.

attrs.problem: Fruit sinking to the bottom of the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid a batter that is too thin; fruit sinks when it has nothing to hold it up.
attrs.fix: Toss the apple pieces in a tablespoon of the measured flour before folding in. Scatter the blackberries on top of the batter rather than folding them in, so they go in closer to the surface.
